answer: Every active head raises the hardware quorum for its entire operator tally. anchor audits control and preserves that tally through wallet and host rotation; at \(k\) heads, comet keeps it active only while \(k^2\) distinct walnut secure modules, exclusively bound to it, sign each fresh challenge together. Ten heads occupy 100 modules, and head ten adds 19. Partial or shared attestations fail. Another operator’s debut occupies one module, so cloning means buying quadratic dedicated hardware, not generating another keypair.
